cells.tense: The feeling has settled into its own depth and is here to be rested in.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Set aside one unhurried stretch and sit with what you feel about someone close, without turning it into a conversation, a plan, or a fix.
cells.core:
You're in a stretch where the feeling has caught up with what you know. The full range of it is available, and you're not in a hurry to move it along — the whole of it can sit there without needing to be said out loud. People notice this and reach for it. You're not bracing for anything.

What this balance is free to do next is let it keep deepening while you're not steering it. Set a real moment aside and sit with what you feel about someone close to you. No conversation, no fix, no task attached. Nothing has to come of it. What shows up when you stay put a while is different from what shows up mid-conversation, and you can find that out by staying put.
cells.sheetLine: The feeling has caught up with what you know.
cells.verb: feeling the whole arc of it, and knowing the feeling itself as already whole
cells.place: at the edge of a finished thing, where what's held is released into what comes next

cells.tense: The ending keeps getting pushed to a point beyond the one you're standing in.
cells.act: hold the first resource in your hand before investing it
cells.ask: Before you put anything more into the thing that's ending, hold the next pay-off in your hand for a day — unspent, uncommitted, not yet named.
cells.core:
You can feel the arc closing, and instead of standing in the close, you're reaching past it — deciding what the end will have meant before the end arrives. Anything unfinished gets covered with an explanation, and the explanation gets treated as the completion. That's a lot of energy spent on a future you can't write in yet, and the present part of the ending goes unfelt.

What's needed is direction that lands where you actually are. Before you hand anything else to this thing, hold the first return you get from it for a day without spending it or naming what it's for. Let it exist in your hand. The end has its own shape, and deciding that shape early is the thing keeping you from living it.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: Catch the first small pull toward something new and follow it one step before you name what it's for.
cells.core:
Where you are in this cycle, the ending has already happened, and your attention hasn't come out of it. You keep describing what closed rather than what's next, and so the completion doesn't quite release you into anything. Nothing has lit up in you toward the next thing yet. The door is behind you; your face is still turned toward it.

Energy is what this needs, and it comes from the smallest available spark rather than a decision. Catch the first pull toward something new and follow it one step before you've decided what it's for. No assignment, no point, just the beginning of a beginning. The new thing will catch once something in you starts moving.

It doesn't have to mean anything.

cells.tense: The completion is being carried out in you without your name on it.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Where a small wrong sits close this week, act on what you sense is right — do it, and don't make the case afterward.
cells.core:
You know what an ending owes people. The felt sense of what's fair — what's been given, what's still owed, when to close a thing cleanly — is operating in you all the time, and the work it does is steady. But you keep the account under the table, and when someone asks how you arrived at a decision, you say it just felt right and stop there.

What returns it to you is doing one small right thing where the compass, not a calculation, is what moves you. Act on it plainly this week. Don't argue the case, don't explain the reasoning, don't defend the call. It was already yours. Doing it without the argument is how you stop being surprised by how well you already understood.

The reader could reasonably say the asks sound like settling for less where the record points to completion; the asks survive that because each one is a small, doable act that teaches them something even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the feeling has settled,' so I've kept it out and let the act carry the settling instead.
